intro.title: Honest Business Partnership Calculator
intro.body: Start with a short business setup, choose quick or full depth, and get a synergy profile with metrics and founder-agreement prompts. Everything stays in your browser.

setup.title: Partnership setup
setup.subtitle: These details tune wording and emphasis later.

result.caption: Business synergy profile
result.shareText: Our partnership profile: {{profile}} ({{score}}%). {{insight}} | Business Partnership — DailyLogic

profiles.clear-bench: A clear bench of ownership and decisions
profiles.pragmatic-duo: Pragmatic partners with a shared compass
profiles.alignment-gap: An alignment gap that needs a talk

insights.dim-opsResilience-high: Your ops/contractual resilience is relatively strong — keep it written, not only remembered.
insights.dim-opsResilience-low: Ops resilience needs reinforcement: who decides, who leads crises, and exit rules.
insights.dim-financialAlignment-high: Financial alignment is relatively strong — rare. Protect it with a monthly money meeting.
insights.dim-financialAlignment-low: Money expectation gaps are a classic partnership breaker. Align thresholds, draws, and splits.
insights.dim-conflictGovernance-high: You can disagree without destroying the business — keep a written decision breaker.
insights.dim-conflictGovernance-low: Without conflict rules, every fight becomes a trust crisis. Set decision rules in advance.
insights.dim-workloadClarity-high: Workload/role clarity is relatively good — verify invisible work is counted too.
insights.dim-workloadClarity-low: Silent pace/load gaps grind partnerships down. Do a light RACI and monthly load check.
insights.overall-strong: Overall alignment looks strong — write it down before pressure stress-tests you.
insights.overall-steady: There's a professional base with soft spots — prioritize one upgrade this week.
insights.overall-developing: Potential exists, but gaps are too big for blind acceleration. Align before scaling.
insights.overall-needs-care: Signals point to high risk. Pause for an honesty round and a minimal document first.
insights.industry-tech: In tech: IP, delivery, and prod transparency are red lines — don't leave them oral.
insights.industry-commerce: In commerce: inventory, vendors, and cashflow break partnerships fast — document money and deps.
insights.industry-services: In services: clients, reputation, and project load are core — define who speaks externally.
insights.industry-food: In food: shifts, service standards, and vendors demand strong daily coordination.
insights.industry-other: Outside classic industries — same principles: clarity, money, decisions, and exit.
insights.equity-equal: Equal equity ≠ equal load. Recheck actual contribution each quarter.
insights.equity-majority: With a clear majority: define minority protections (veto on critical topics).
insights.equity-complex: With complex splits: simplify update/vesting rules — complexity without docs is a trap.

tips.tip-decision-rights: Write a decision matrix: solo / together / majority required.
tips.tip-crisis-owner: Name a crisis owner and deputy — before the incident.
tips.tip-exit-clause: Define a basic exit/buyout: notice, valuation, payment.
tips.tip-monthly-money-meeting: A fixed monthly money meeting: burn, commitments, near-term decisions.
tips.tip-expense-thresholds: Set an expense threshold for solo spend vs mandatory alignment.
tips.tip-sweat-vs-cash: Track sweat vs cash contribution — so it doesn't become old resentment.
tips.tip-deadlock-rule: Set a deadlock breaker: advisor, controlled coin-flip, or rotating chair.
tips.tip-feedback-ritual: Biweekly feedback ritual: 20 minutes, facts first, interpretation second.
tips.tip-no-side-channels: No side-channels on critical decisions — everything at the shared table.
tips.tip-raci-lite: A light RACI for only 5 critical processes. Not a 40-page wiki.
tips.tip-capacity-check: Weekly: open capacity % per partner — no heroics.
tips.tip-invisible-work-log: Log one week of invisible work — then redistribute.
tips.tip-founders-cadence: A fixed weekly founders sync — even 30 minutes — beats chaotic chat.

agreement.agree-exit-and-buyout: Basic exit & buyout clause (notice, valuation, payment schedule).
agreement.agree-ip-ownership: Ownership of IP/assets/client relationships and assignment to the venture.
agreement.agree-compensation-policy: Salary/dividend/expense reimbursement policy and approval thresholds.
agreement.agree-conflict-escalation: Escalation path and mediation/arbitration on deadlock.
agreement.agree-time-commitment: Minimum time commitment and updates when capacity changes.

decide-under-pressure.prompt: Under pressure we can still decide without freezing or exploding.

failure-ownership.prompt: When something fails — ownership is clear, without blame games.

byIndustry.tech: When a feature/release fails — ownership is clear, without bug-blame ping-pong.
byIndustry.commerce: When inventory/shipping fails — it's clear who closes with vendor and customer.
byIndustry.services: When a client project breaks — it's clear who talks to the client and who fixes inside.
byIndustry.food: When service/shift collapses — it's clear who pulls the rope in real time.
byIndustry.other: When something fails in the field — ownership and closure are clear.

roles-clear.prompt: Roles and authority between us are clear enough for day-to-day work.

exit-talked.prompt: We've talked honestly about a possible exit — not only the success dream.

red-lines-named.prompt: Red lines were named out loud (money, ethics, time) — not just "we'll see".

crisis-playbook.prompt: We know who leads in an ops crisis, even without a dramatic meeting.

byIndustry.tech: In a prod/security incident — we know who leads comms and who fixes.
byIndustry.commerce: In a supplier/warehouse crisis — we know who decides pause/discounts/compensation.
byIndustry.services: In a major client crisis — we know who leads the call and who backs resources.
byIndustry.food: In a kitchen/staffing crisis — we know who closes menu/shifts immediately.
byIndustry.other: In an ops crisis — we know who leads without endless debate.

ip-or-assets-clarity.prompt: It's clear what belongs to the partnership vs personal (assets / know-how / relationships).

byIndustry.tech: It's clear who owns code, data, and IP — even if someone exits.
byIndustry.commerce: It's clear who owns brand, audience, and critical suppliers.
byIndustry.services: It's clear who owns client relationships, methods, and materials.
byIndustry.food: It's clear who owns recipes, suppliers, and brand name.
byIndustry.other: It's clear what belongs to the partnership vs personal assets.

vendors-and-deps.prompt: External dependencies (vendors/contractors) are managed transparently between partners.

byIndustry.tech: Work with freelancers/tech vendors is transparent to both partners.
byIndustry.commerce: Supplier and inventory relationships are transparent — no side deals.
byIndustry.services: Subcontractors are approved and visible to partners.
byIndustry.food: Food and external service vendors are managed with partner transparency.
byIndustry.other: External dependencies are managed transparently between partners.

money-talks-honest.prompt: Money talks are honest — even when the numbers aren't flattering.

first-money-vs-sweat.prompt: We align on early cash, sweat equity, and asymmetric contribution.

equity-feels-fair.prompt: Equity/profit split feels fair enough relative to actual contribution.

burn-and-runway.prompt: There's transparency on burn and runway — no end-of-month surprises.

salary-vs-reinvest.prompt: We agree when to take salary/dividends vs reinvest.

expense-authority.prompt: It's clear up to what amount one can spend alone vs must align.

investor-or-debt-views.prompt: We're aligned on fundraising/debt — or have a process to decide.

profit-distribution-rules.prompt: Profit distribution rules are written or at least explicit.

disagree-then-decide.prompt: After disagreement we know how to close a decision and move on.

ego-in-meetings.prompt: Ego doesn't block good decisions — even when it's hard to swallow.

feedback-without-war.prompt: We can give sharp feedback without starting a world war.

deadlock-break.prompt: There's a deadlock breaker (tie-break / advisor / rotation) — not only hope.

client-or-team-conflict.prompt: Client/team conflict is handled as partners, not two camps.

byIndustry.tech: Product/customer priority fights close as a founding team — not two camps.
byIndustry.commerce: Customer/returns conflict is handled together — not good-cop/bad-cop theater.
byIndustry.services: When a client pushes — we align before answering, not after.
byIndustry.food: A customer complaint/public review is handled as one front.
byIndustry.other: External conflict is handled as partners, not camps.

apology-and-course-correct.prompt: Apology comes with course-correction — not only a polite email.

transparency-default.prompt: Transparency is the default (info, risks, mistakes) — not a reward.

pace-mismatch.prompt: When work pace differs — we talk before frustration explodes.

invisible-labor.prompt: Invisible work (admin, follow-ups, firefighting) is recognized, not only done.

who-owns-delivery.prompt: It's clear who owns delivery — not "everyone" and then no one.

byIndustry.tech: It's clear who owns technical delivery/release — including after hours.
byIndustry.commerce: It's clear who owns end-to-end supply/fulfillment targets.
byIndustry.services: It's clear who owns client delivery and who holds the timeline.
byIndustry.food: It's clear who owns service-quality standards every shift.
byIndustry.other: It's clear who owns real delivery end to end.

time-off-without-guilt.prompt: We can take time off without feeling like we betrayed the partnership.

hiring-and-firing-views.prompt: We're aligned on hiring and letting go of people/contractors.

communication-cadence.prompt: We have enough communication cadence — not only chaotic chat threads.

vision-still-shared.prompt: We still share strategic direction — or know how to realign when we diverge.
